author: GamingBolt
description:
The art behind delivering bad news is to lace it with something good. Something positive that people, especially those who like to own the things they buy, can find hope in. So naturally, when PlayStation announced the end of new game disc production from January 2028 onwards, effectively ripping the Band-Aid off in this highly digital age, it offered nothing even remotely hopeful as a make-do. It even crammed in the announcement of the PS3 and PS Vita stores shutting down, and revealed the underwhelming Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 (the bad one) for PlayStation Plus in July. A triple whammy like no other.

Fans responded in kind with a continuing firestorm on social media, be it in tweets, YouTube videos, you name it. Well, with its latest financial report available, the top brass at Sony Group Corporation responded, acknowledging the “various opinions” and “strong views” that fans have to offer.
title: PlayStation Heard the Physical Disc Backlash - And Is Moving Ahead Anyway

author: GamingBolt
description:
A role-playing game, by tradition, doesn't have to be one where your choices impact the world. And yet, choice and consequence are fundamental elements that have driven the genre for so long. Not the choices in tactics, party members, equipment or abilities, but what defines the journey in your own mind.

The choice to nuke Megaton in Fallout 3. The choice to bring Anabelle's bones to Graham in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Even the choice of where to send Jacky after the pivotal heist in Cyberpunk 2077. These can have pivotal, long-term effects on the story, sometimes in ways that won't be obvious within the confines of the game. They don't just stay with you because they're significant, but because you made them and had to live with the consequences forever (or at least until you reload and try something else).
title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Does What Most Games Won't - Make Every Choice Matter

author: GamingBolt
description:
Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy marks the series’ most significant reinvention yet. Rats are nowhere to be seen, and stealth no longer dominates every encounter. Instead, a pair of new protagonists bring intense swordplay and light RPG progression. 

Beneath the sweeping changes, however, is the same focus on environmental storytelling and light-based puzzles that defined its predecessors. Ahead of release, here are fifteen things you need to know.
title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy - 15 Things You ABSOLUTELY Need To Know Before You Buy
